= Aura Graph Analytics: GraphSAGE embedding training via sessions



This Jupyter notebook is hosted
https://github.com/neo4j/graph-data-science-client/blob/main/examples/graph-analytics-serverless-standalone-graphsage-unsupervised.ipynb[here]
in the Neo4j Graph Data Science Client Github repository.

The notebook shows how to use the `graphdatascience` Python library to
train an unsupervised GraphSAGE model on Cora and compute node
embeddings on an Aura Graph Analytics (AGA) Session, using the typed
`gds.graph++_++sage.unsupervised` endpoints.

== Prerequisites

This notebook requires having the Aura Graph Analytics
https://neo4j.com/docs/aura/graph-analytics/#aura-gds-serverless[feature]
enabled for your Neo4j Aura project, and a session backed by the *Python
runtime*.

You also need to have the `graphdatascience` Python library installed,
version `2.1` or later.

[source, python, role=no-test]
----
%pip install "graphdatascience>=2.1" python-dotenv matplotlib numpy

== Credentials

[source, python, role=no-test]
----
import os

from dotenv import load_dotenv

# This allows to load required secrets from `.env` file in local directory
load_dotenv(".env")
----

== Aura API credentials

[source, python, role=no-test]
----
from graphdatascience.session import AuraAPICredentials, GdsSessions

api_credentials = AuraAPICredentials(
    client_id=os.environ["CLIENT_ID"],
    client_secret=os.environ["CLIENT_SECRET"],
    # If your account is a member of several projects, you must also specify the project ID to use
    project_id=os.environ.get("PROJECT_ID", None),
)

sessions = GdsSessions(api_credentials=api_credentials)
----

== Creating a new session

A new session is created by calling `sessions.get++_++or++_++create()`
with a representative name, the session memory, the cloud location, and
a time-to-live (TTL), which ensures that the session is automatically
deleted after being unused for the set time, to avoid incurring costs.

[source, python, role=no-test]
----
from datetime import timedelta

from graphdatascience.session import CloudLocation, SessionMemory

# Explicitly define the size of the session
memory = SessionMemory.m_4GB

# Specify your cloud location
cloud_location = CloudLocation("gcp", "europe-west1")

# Create a GDS session!
gds = sessions.get_or_create(
    # we give it a representative name
    session_name="graphsage-unsupervised",
    memory=memory,
    ttl=timedelta(minutes=30),
    cloud_location=cloud_location,
)

# Verify the connectivity. Hints towards TLS or firewall issues if this fails directly after get_or_create
gds.verify_connectivity()
----

== Load Cora

The Cora citation dataset ships with the client and is loaded directly
into the session, with `CITES` relationships treated as *undirected* so
the random walks used by unsupervised GraphSAGE can traverse citations
in both directions.

[source, python, role=no-test]
----
gds.graph.drop("cora", fail_if_missing=False)
gds.model.delete("gds_demo_graphsage_unsupervised", fail_if_missing=False)

G = gds.graph.datasets.load_cora(undirected=True)
print("Loaded graph:", G.name())
----

== Train GraphSAGE (Unsupervised)

`gds.graph++_++sage.unsupervised.train` submits the training job, blocks
until completion (with progress reporting), and returns the trained
model together with a train summary result. `featureProperties` selects
the node properties used as input features (here Cora's `features`
vector). `nodeLabels` and `relationshipTypes` default to `++*++`
(project everything).

[source, python, role=no-test]
----
model, train_result = gds.graph_sage.unsupervised.train(
    G,
    model_name="gds_demo_graphsage_unsupervised",
    feature_properties=["features"],
    epochs=10,
    embedding_dimension=64,
    learning_rate=0.001,
    num_neighbors=[25, 10],
    activation_function="relu",
    aggregator="mean",
    num_walks=10,
    walk_depth=3,
    random_seed=42,
)

print("Trained model:", model.name())
----

[source, python, role=no-test]
----
train_result
----

== Run Inference

`gds.graph++_++sage.unsupervised.stream` runs the predict job against
the stored model and streams the results. Unsupervised GraphSAGE
produces a node embedding per node (rather than class predictions).
Inference projects the same `featureProperties` the model was trained
on.

[source, python, role=no-test]
----
embeddings_df = gds.graph_sage.unsupervised.stream(
    G,
    model_name=model.name(),
    feature_properties=["features"],
    random_seed=42,
)

print("Columns:", list(embeddings_df.columns))
embeddings_df
----

== Visualize embeddings

[source, python, role=no-test]
----
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

# colour each paper by its `subject` to see how embeddings cluster
subjects = gds.graph.node_properties.stream(G, "subject")
embeddings_df = embeddings_df.merge(subjects, on="nodeId")

# project the 64-dim embeddings to 2D with an SVD (no extra dependencies needed)
X = np.stack(embeddings_df["embedding"].to_numpy())
X = X - X.mean(axis=0)
U, _, _ = np.linalg.svd(X, full_matrices=False)
embeddings_df["x"], embeddings_df["y"] = U[:, 0], U[:, 1]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 6))
for subject in sorted(embeddings_df["subject"].unique()):
    part = embeddings_df[embeddings_df["subject"] == subject]
    ax.scatter(part["x"], part["y"], s=25, label=f"subject {subject}")
ax.set_title("GraphSAGE embeddings of Cora papers")
ax.set_xlabel("component 1")
ax.set_ylabel("component 2")
ax.legend()
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
----

== Cleanup

After the analysis is done, we delete the trained model and the graph,
and then delete the session. Deleting the session releases all resources
associated with it, and stops incurring costs.

[source, python, role=no-test]
----
gds.model.delete("gds_demo_graphsage_unsupervised", fail_if_missing=False)

G.drop(fail_if_missing=False)
----

[source, python, role=no-test]
----
sessions.delete(session_name="graphsage-unsupervised")
----
